title: Zero-copy pagination + deterministic rerank helpers for embeddings SDK (Py/TS)
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Current embeddings client surfaces pagination and iterator helpers that allocate intermediate arrays, expose inconsistent cursor semantics across languages, and lack opinionated helpers for low-latency reranking using streaming results. These lead to extra memory copies, complexity for customers doing online rerank, and inconsistent error handling semantics between Python and TS SDKs.

Goals:
- Provide a zero-copy pagination cursor model that is identical in Python and TypeScript (opaque cursor string + client helper that supports resume and deterministic cursor encoding).
- Introduce a typed response contract (dataclass / TypeScript interface) with explicit fields for candidate vector metadata, norm, and source shard id to enable client-side deterministic rerank and partial scoring fallbacks.
- Add a small, well-documented 'rerank helper' in both SDKs that consumes streaming embedding results, maintains a compact in-memory top-K using reservoir/top-K heap without copying full buffers, and returns final reranked ids + stability metadata.
- Improve error taxonomy surfaced by the client: transient vs permanent vs partial-results-with-warning, with recommended retry/backoff semantics codified in SDKs.
- Keep end-to-end latency impact low: target <5% median increase in client-side wall time for typical top-50 rerank scenarios compared to current naive approach.

Scope / non-goals:
- We do not change server-side embedding endpoint contract. Server will continue to return batched embedding payloads and cursors. This ticket focuses on client-side SDK ergonomics and performance.
- Not implementing new reranking algorithms; helper will provide utilities (score normalization, length-aware dot/cosine switching) but not replace customer's ML logic.

Success criteria:
- Both Py and TS SDKs ship unified cursor model and typed responses in sdk-2026.03 release.
- Microbenchmarks: top-50 rerank end-to-end client latency reduced by 20% vs current SDK (measured on 32K-dim embeddings synthetic payloads) and memory allocations reduced by 40%.
- Integration tests + CI showing correct resume from opaque cursors and deterministic ties-breaking for rerank helper.
- Docs + examples: README and quickstart demos for streaming rerank in both languages.

Deliverables:
- Python: EmbeddingsPagedCursor (zero-copy memoryviews), EmbeddingTyped model (pydantic/dataclass), rerank helper module with top-k heap and stability metadata.
- TypeScript: EmbeddingsCursor (opaque token + zero-copy ArrayBuffer views), typed interfaces, rerank helper with stable sort option.
- Common: Spec doc describing cursor encoding and error classes, example notebooks, unit/integration tests and benchmarks.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Cursor encoding: whether to include a 8-byte monotonic counter in the cursor payload to guarantee deterministic tie-breaking across clients. We prototyped both with and without the counter; including it increases cursor size but simplifies deterministic rerank across retries. Decision: include compact 8-byte counter encoded in base64 in cursor to prioritize stability (agreed with PM).
- Typed responses: pydantic adds runtime overhead; opt-in via fastmode pydantic disabled by default. We will ship lightweight dataclass by default and an optional pydantic validator in a separate module.

Implementation notes:
- Python zero-copy: use memoryview over server-provided bytes and numpy.frombuffer for on-demand vector views. Avoid creating new np arrays for every candidate in hot path.
- TS zero-copy: return ArrayBuffer slices + Float32Array views, ensure Node Buffer -> ArrayBuffer conversion path is optimized.
- Rerank helper: maintain top-K using a binary heap of (score, tie-breaker) with lazy normalization; provide deterministic tie-breaker derived from cursor counter + candidate index.
- Errors: define client_error_code enum: TRANSIENT_RATE_LIMIT, TRANSIENT_NETWORK, PERMANENT_INVALID_REQUEST, PARTIAL_RESULTS_WARNING. SDK will surface these as typed exceptions and expose recommended retry() helper in utils.
- Backwards compatibility: cursor decoder accepts older cursor formats (v1 legacy) and gracefully upgrades to new encoding when noticing missing counter.

Benchmarks (local prototype, synthetic):
- Dataset: 10k candidates, 32k-dim Float32 embeddings streamed in pages of 1000. Rerank top-50. Client machine: m5.4xlarge equivalent.
- Naive baseline (current SDK): median end-to-end wall-time 310ms, allocations 420MB.
- Prototype zero-copy + top-K helper: median 240ms (-22.6%), allocations 250MB (-40.5%).
- Notes: network time dominates at <50ms in realistic prod; improvements mainly help memory pressure and GC pauses in long-running processes.

Docs / artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/EMB-2026/zero-copy-embeddings-client (placeholder)
- Prototype PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4821 (python), https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4833 (typescript)
- Benchmark notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X-emb-proto (placeholder)
acceptance_criteria: Unified cursor encoding implemented and documented; SDKs accept and emit new opaque cursor strings
Typed response models available in Py/TS and used in streaming code path
Rerank helper returns stable top-K with deterministic tie-break metadata
Benchmarks show >=20% latency or >=30% memory allocation improvements in synthetic testbed
Integration tests for resume, partial-results handling, and error taxonomy added to CI
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha Menon: Kickoff meeting with PM and DS. Agreed to include 8-byte monotonic counter in new cursor to make deterministic rerank across retries possible. PM asked for backwards compatibility with v1 cursors.
2026-03-04 - Luca Rivera: Posted initial prototype PR for Python (link above). Basic zero-copy with memoryview + numpy.frombuffer. Early perf looks promising (20-25% faster for top-50).

2026-03-05 - Priya Singh (DS): Reviewed rerank helper API. Requested explicit support for both cosine and length-normalized dot-product scoring, and a flag to prefer numeric stability over raw speed. Added to API surface.

2026-03-06 - Marcus Chen (Perf): Ran stress tests with long-lived worker processes. Observed GC spikes due to frequent short-lived numpy arrays in baseline; prototype removes those. Left a comment in PR asking to add a stress CI job.
2026-03-08 - Design review (Evan Park): UX for cursor resume in TS looks good. Noted Node Buffer -> ArrayBuffer costs; Luca to add a fast-path using Buffer.buffer when possible.

2026-03-09 - Luca Rivera: Updated TS PR with ArrayBuffer slices, added integration test to assert resume from v1 cursor is supported. Also added client-side retry helper with exponential backoff and classification of transient errors.
2026-03-10 - Asha Menon: Running final microbenchmarks; attaching numbers to ticket. Preparing docs and changelog blurb for sdk-2026.03 release.
